resources.string: This file is not text. Nothing is shown rather than a screen of unreadable characters.
Compare this against the value published by the vendor. A firmware image that differs by one byte is not the image you meant to install.
That path leaves the share and was refused.
Something with that name is already there.
This folder cannot be written to.
A name cannot be empty and cannot contain / \\ : * ? " < > |
A folder cannot be copied into itself.
Switch on at least one protocol below.
If a client cannot connect, the network is isolating its devices from one another. That is a setting on the access point, not on this phone.

Android runs apps without privileges, and the system refuses to bind ports below 1024. TFTP cannot use 69, FTP cannot use 21 and SSH cannot use 22 — no app on an unrooted phone can. Clients that let you name a port work normally. Clients that do not, including some network hardware over TFTP, cannot reach this server.
On a mobile network your phone often has a publicly routable IPv6 address. Wi-Fi only keeps the share off it.
The share will also be reachable over the mobile network, which may put it on the public internet.
The usual way this goes wrong is not an attack. It is finishing the job, pocketing the phone, and leaving a write-enabled share running on a customer network all afternoon.
Keep the CPU awake while serving
Without this a long transfer stalls when the screen goes off.
A client can write files without logging in. Anyone who can reach this port can put a file on your phone.
What switches and routers use for firmware and configs. No authentication exists in the protocol.
TFTP has no passwords and no user names — none are defined in the protocol. Switching this on means anyone who can reach the port can write to the share.
1468 bytes is the largest that still fits one Ethernet frame. The protocol default of 512 is roughly three times slower.
How many blocks may be sent before an acknowledgement. A window of 1 caps throughput at one block per round trip. Clients that do not know the option simply do not use it.
Widely supported, and readable by anyone on the network unless TLS is switched on.
A passive transfer opens a second connection on one of these ports. A fixed range is what makes the server work through a firewall.

Uses a certificate this device generates for itself, so every client will warn that it cannot verify who it is talking to — and it is right. What this does buy is that passwords and file contents are no longer readable by others on the same network. For a connection that is authenticated as well as encrypted, use SFTP.
Encrypted and authenticated. The right choice on any network you do not control.
OpenSSH 9 and later send an \"scp\" command over SFTP, so modern clients need only the subsystem above. Cisco IOS and similar gear still speak the original SCP protocol and need this.
This server offers files and nothing else. No shell is available, whoever logs in.
Compare this with the fingerprint your client shows the first time it connects. If it matches, the connection reached this phone and not something in between.

Every client that has connected before will refuse the next connection and report that the host identification has changed. Each one has to have its stored entry removed by hand. Do this only if you believe the current key has been copied off the device.
Ports below 1024 cannot be used. Pick a higher one.
No Wi-Fi address. Connect to a network, or change \"Listen on\".
The device could not produce a TLS certificate. Switch FTPS off to start without it.
It did not start. The log has the details.
FTP and SSH ask for these. TFTP cannot — the protocol has no notion of a user.
No accounts yet. Without one, only anonymous FTP can be used, and only if you switch it on.
Leave empty for the whole share. A switch that only ever fetches firmware has no reason to see the rest.

Passwords are stored in clear text in this app\'s private storage, so they can be read back when you need to type one into a client. A hashed password could never be shown again — which in practice is how people end up choosing \"1234\".
One OpenSSH line per key. This is the only credential here that cannot be read off the screen by someone standing behind you.
Paste the line from your id_ed25519.pub or id_rsa.pub
Nothing yet. Connections and transfers appear here while the servers run.
